title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages): P is a combinatorial polygon (a 'polygone combinatoire'), with edges a and vertices s. A 'P-weighted map' (carte P-pondérée) is a map on a surface whose faces are copies of P. Each face edge carries a type a, an edge of P, and the face's cyclic structure is induced from that of P. The group Π_P^τ is defined in (62) by generators τ_a, involutions indexed by the edges of P. Judging from the n=3 case, which Grothendieck explicitly generalizes, it is presumably the free product of copies of Z/2, one per edge; for n=3 this is his cartographic group C_2 = Z/2*Z/2*Z/2. Previous page, equivalence (101): X ↦ R(X), the set of faces of X, with τ_a sending a face to its neighbour across its a-edge. This gives an equivalence between finite P-weighted maps and finite Π_P^τ-sets on which every τ_a acts without fixed points. Equivalence (102): X ↦ R^+(X), the set of 'direct' faces, gives an equivalence between oriented finite P-weighted maps and finite Π_P-sets.

This page makes a canonicity remark:
- Π_P^τ and (101) need no data beyond P. Π_P^τ is defined purely combinatorially by (62), with no basepoint P_∞ in Σ_P^*.
- Π_P and (102) need an orientation of P. With it, Π_P can be introduced as π_1(Σ_P^*, P_∞). Here Σ_P is the double of P, a sphere with the n vertices as marked points, i.e. P^1 with n points; Σ_P^* is the complement of the vertices; P_∞ is a base point in the 'direct' hemisphere.
- Π_P can also be defined canonically, without choosing ω, as the kernel of Π_P^τ → {±1}, τ_a ↦ −1, giving the exact sequence (103): 1 → Π_P → Π_P^τ → {±1} → 1.
- Even so, the functor (102) itself depends on the orientation, since one must decide which faces are 'direct'.

A quasi-inverse of (102) comes from Galois theory of étale covers (104). Finite Π_P-sets correspond to finite covers of Σ_P that may be ramified over the vertices and are étale over Σ_P^*. For such a cover X → Σ_P, pull back the canonical map on Σ_P: the tiling of the sphere by the two hemispheres P and its mirror, which plays the role of the universal oriented P-weighted map. This yields the oriented P-weighted map sought.

The next page treats the non-oriented quasi-inverse of (101) by 'twisting' C by the orientation torsor ω. It also refers to generalizing §5, which relates P-weighted maps to maps all of whose faces are n-gons.

Overall this is the n-gon generalization of the dessins d'enfants / cartographic-group dictionary. The case n=3 gives maps and hypermaps, with π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) = F_2 as the index-2 subgroup of Z/2*Z/2*Z/2.
errors: No mathematical error. Well-definedness of (103) needs every relation in (62) to have even length in the τ's. This is automatic for a free product of Z/2's, and also for Coxeter-type relations (τ_aτ_b)^m.

Identifying the kernel with π_1(Σ_P^*, P_∞) as an actual isomorphism uses the orientation, to place P_∞ in the 'direct' cell. Grothendieck states this correctly. Only the subgroup is canonical; its identification with the topological π_1 and the functor (102) are not.

ideas.what: Finite P-weighted maps (faces modelled on an n-gon P) ↔ finite sets with fixed-point-free involutions τ_a indexed by the edges of P, i.e. Π_P^τ-sets
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial maps / polygonal tilings as permutation representations of (extended) polygon groups, a free product of Z/2's; generalized cartographic groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978) for maps and triangle groups; Bryant–Singerman (1985) for extended groups and non-orientable maps; Cori/Walsh (1975) for hypermaps; Grothendieck's cartographic groups (Esquisse, 1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), cartographic groups C_2, C_2^+, n=3 case; the general n-gon version is not developed there as far as I know

ideas.what: Canonicity remark: the extended group Π_P^τ needs no basepoint or orientation; the oriented group Π_P is canonically the kernel of τ_a ↦ −1, but the equivalence with oriented maps depends on the orientation
ideas.modern_name: Index-2 orientation subgroup of a reflection-type group; orientation torsor; π_1 of the real orbifold P versus π_1 of its complex double
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (orbifold covering theory, Thurston; reflection groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses C_2 vs C_2^+ and orientation-dependence in passing; unsure of an explicit statement

ideas.what: Quasi-inverse via Galois theory: Π_P-sets ↔ finite covers of Σ_P ≅ P^1 ramified only over the n vertices; oriented maps obtained by pulling back the canonical two-cell 'universal' map on Σ_P
ideas.modern_name: Riemann existence theorem / Grothendieck's dessin correspondence generalized to n branch points (n-pointed dessins, 'n-gonal' dessins)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse) for n=3; generalizations folklore (e.g. Zapponi and others on dessins with more branch points)

missed.claim: The page is an expository canonicity remark within Grothendieck's unpublished n-gon generalization of the cartographic-group dictionary. The dictionary itself is standard and known to specialists in its n=3 form. The only mildly distinctive point, developed on the next page, is the habit of handling orientation-dependence by twisting C into C(ω) by the orientation torsor. It is not a new result, though it is a characteristic stylistic device.
missed.quote: mais il reste que le choix d'un foncteur (102) dépend du choix d'une orientation sur P
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It documents that Grothendieck in 1981 worked with arbitrary n-gons, i.e. covers of P^1 branched over n points, and not only Belyi's three-point case. It also shows him tracking the dependence on orientation (complex conjugation) carefully. This is of historical rather than mathematical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping on canonicity in a known correspondence: maps ↔ permutation representations of free products of Z/2's, and branched covers of P^1. It is historically consistent with the Esquisse and adds nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'des poly-combinatoire P' is more likely 'du polygone combinatoire P' (or 'polyg. combinatoire').
'sans choix de ce' should read 'sans choix de ω' (the orientation).
Groups are written Π_P, Π_P^τ (capital pi) in the image, consistent with the previous page.
'si on a un tel rev. X de Σ_P, l'image inverse de la carte canonique sur Σ_P (jouant le rôle de carte P-pondérée orientée universelle)': 'canonique' is an insertion replacing a struck word.
In (104) 'étale' is struck after 'rev.'; the header reads 'revêtements ramifiés finis de Σ_P, étales au dessus de Σ_P^*'.
